alignments.note: Coordinator and connective written together at the recast clause's left edge are one rendering of the single waw, headed on the coordinator (rule 55); marking *so* added under rule 30 was the competing reading, and the ASV italic corroborates neither by rule 7.
Causative rendered as *cause ... to bear*; head on the lexical second verb (rule 44).
Object marker with no English of its own (rule 16).
The rectum keeps only *guilt*, the word the ASV writes for its lexeme. Rule 19 hands a rectum the relational *of* or a preposition the ASV recasts it with, and *that bringeth* is neither.

Relative supplied for a clause the Hebrew does not write. The antecedent is written and the clause is juxtaposed to it, so rule 46 does not license the word and rules 30 and 55 leave it added; it is not folded into the construct noun beside it, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and*.

*bringeth* predicates an event of the iniquity rather than naming it, so it is a supplied lexical participle inside a nominal recasting and is added, exactly as *done* is in `חֲמַס אֶרֶץ` → *violence done to the land* (rule 20). Giving *that bringeth* to אַשְׁמָה as the construct relation's recast expression was the competing reading and was what the earlier alignment took, but rule 19's recasting reaches a preposition and not a supplied predication, and rule 20 states the boundary in its own terms.
Temporal preposition before an infinitive construct takes the *when* (rule 52).
The suffix on the infinitive construct is its subject and takes the English subject pronoun (rule 18).
Object marker with no English of its own (rule 16).
Head on *holy*, since *things* alone is any thing (rule 31).
Explicit subject pronoun takes only its own English (rule 20).
Articleless attributive participle recast as a relative clause keeps the supplied relative (rule 41).

review_notes: *and so* is given whole to the waw under rule 55; marking *so* added under rule 30 remains defensible.

Corrected: *that bringeth* is no longer read as the construct relation's rendering. Rule 19 gives a rectum the relational *of* or a preposition the ASV recasts the relation with, while rule 20 rules that a supplied lexical participle inside a nominal recasting is added — *violence done to the land* leaves *done* added because it predicates an event rather than naming the thing. So אַשְׁמָה keeps *guilt* alone and the supplied relative and participle are their own added units.
The added pieces are kept apart under rule 2, the relative answering to rules 46 and 55 and the participle to rule 20; lumping them as one supplied relative frame is the near alternative.
